title: CARBCOMN - Dataset of Early Research Outcomes - Mix Design of 3D-printable Mixes Based on Industrial Slags
question: How do mix composition and material structure jointly affect printability and strength?
publisher: Lorika, Denis Ayena (Department of Structural Engineering and Building Materials, Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium)
variables_and_units: rheology, strength, micro-CT descriptors and thermal response
validation_design: mixes and specimen batches Verify identifiers before allocating groups; the partition is not executed or frozen by this acquisition.
author_preprocessing: Original workbooks contain mix/strength, rheology, TGA and micro-CT descriptors. Micro-CT workbook is a derived product, not full voxel tomography.
prior_analysis_and_limits: Group by formulation and specimen batch. Do not use derived strength predictors calculated from the response as independent inputs.
missingness: Native blanks, sentinels, absent records and source quality flags are preserved. No imputation performed by the curator. Exact missingness semantics come from source dictionaries/headers; no universal missing-value rule is imposed.
calibration: Use the retained source calibration files/standards and instrument metadata where provided. Absence of an explicit calibration record is not replaced by an assumed calibration.

sheets.name: AC_IFSTTAR
first_rows: Absorption Capacity of stinox after 2h of soaking

eligibility.novelty: no unseen-law guarantee; independent adjudication required

exposure: Open source-aware; source literature and supplied analyses accessible
unit_interpretation: Use exact source field/sheet/channel labels and units in source_evidence and per-file reports; unknown units remain unresolved, not inferred from a variable name.
